html:
The Summer Olympic Games held in Melbourne from November to December 1956. They were the first held in the Southern Hemisphere, and the first outside Europe and North America.

Strict Australian rules on importing horses meant the riding events had to be held in Stockholm, months earlier. The Games themselves came in a tense year. The Netherlands, Spain and Switzerland stayed away in protest at the Soviet crushing of the Hungarian revolution. Egypt, Iraq and Lebanon boycotted over the Suez Crisis, and China withdrew over Taiwan.

In the pool the anger boiled over. A water polo match between Hungary and the Soviet Union turned violent and became known as the Blood in the Water match. Hungary won and went on to take gold.

The Soviet Union topped the medal table, and Australia did well at home, with the sprinter Betty Cuthbert winning three golds. At the closing ceremony athletes walked together, mixed, rather than in national teams, an idea suggested by a teenage spectator. That custom has lasted ever since.
sum: The Summer Olympic Games held in Melbourne from November to December 1956. They were the first held in the Southern Hemisphere, and the first outside Europe and North America.
